title: Morphisms of algebraic spaces to affine schemes are determined by global functions
statement: Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-pc-scheme], and let $T$ be an affine scheme, that is, a scheme isomorphic to a spectrum of a commutative ring [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The map $$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(X,T)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ring}}(\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T),\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)),\qquad f\longmapsto f^\sharp$$ is bijective. Morphisms on the left are natural transformations of the representing fppf sheaves; homomorphisms on the right preserve the unit. Global functions on $X$ are global sections of its small etale structure sheaf. No quasi-compactness, separation or cohomological hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $p:h_U\to X$ using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. By [lem-a1-etale-atlas-presentation], the scheme $R=U\times_XU$ with projections $s,t$ represents the relation of sections of $U$ having the same image in $X$, and the sheafified quotient $Q=U/R$ is canonically $X$, compatibly with $p$.

source.place: Tag 05Z1 (lemma-morphism-to-affine-scheme), choose a presentation; spaces.tex Tag 0262 (lemma-space-presentation).

proof.text: Write $A=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ and $B=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Let $\varphi:A\to B$ preserve the unit. Since $T$ is affine, choose $T\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A$ (transport any spectrum presentation along its isomorphism on global sections). The scheme affine-target lemma gives a unique $g:U\to T$ with $g^\sharp=p^\sharp\circ\varphi$. Both $U$ and the relation scheme $R$ may be non-affine.

source.place: Tag 05Z1, construction of g from the composite on global sections; schemes.tex Tag 01I1 (lemma-morphism-into-affine).

proof.text: Because $p\circ s=p\circ t$, functoriality of pullback gives $s^\sharp\circ p^\sharp=t^\sharp\circ p^\sharp$. Thus $(g\circ s)^\sharp=(g\circ t)^\sharp$. The uniqueness part of the scheme affine-target lemma on $R$ gives $g\circ s=g\circ t$. The representable functors $h_R,h_U,h_T$ are fppf sheaves: an fppf covering is an fpqc covering [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc], and scheme morphisms agreeing on overlaps glue uniquely along fpqc coverings [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent]. Apply the sheafified-relation coequalizer lemma with $h_R\rightrightarrows h_U$, the quotient $Q$ supplied in step 1, and target the fppf sheaf $h_T$. It gives a unique $f:X\simeq Q\to T$ with $f\circ p=g$.

source.place: Tag 05Z1, equality on R and descent to X=U/R; groupoids.tex definition-quotient-sheaf and the following coequalizer paragraph. Representables are fppf sheaves: descent.tex Tag 023Q (lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms) with topologies.tex Tag 022C.

proof.text: The restriction $p^\sharp:B\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ is injective: a global section is a compatible family on the small etale site. If two such families agree on $U$, then on any etale scheme chart $W\to X$ they agree after restriction to the etale covering $W\times_XU\to W$. The sheaf separatedness axiom makes their components on $W$ equal. This proves injectivity on families. Consequently $p^\sharp\circ f^\sharp=g^\sharp=p^\sharp\circ\varphi$ implies $f^\sharp=\varphi$.

If $f_1,f_2:X\to T$ induce the same homomorphism on global functions, then $f_1\circ p,f_2\circ p:U\to T$ have the same pullback and are equal by the scheme affine-target lemma. Uniqueness of factorization through the coequalizer $h_U\to Q\simeq X$ gives $f_1=f_2$. This proves both injectivity and surjectivity of the stated map, without any compactness, separation, or cohomological assumption.

source.place: Tag 05Z1, last sentence (uniqueness of f from uniqueness of g).
